title: Headline went too far
article: A letter from John Zyp, Edmonton.

It seems to be a fact that Kasim Cakmak was pepper-sprayed and that he died but your own report indicates that it is not clear that the pepper spray caused his death. It also is not clear that vital data could have saved Kasim.

Headlines -- as you well know -- are powerful tools for grabbing attention. "Pepper spray death: Vital data could have saved man," certainly makes one sit up and take notice. Verbal punches like that, however, may do injustice to the essence of the story.

It seems to be a fact that Kasim Cakmak was pepper-sprayed and that he died but your own report indicates that it is not clear that the pepper spray caused his death. It also is not clear that vital data could have saved Kasim. It probably is more accurate that it may have saved him.
As a member of the Regional Mental Health Advisory Committee, I am deeply concerned about tragic events like this but also about the way they are reported.
I commend you for what appears to be careful coverage of the incident. Please be just as careful with your headlines.
